learn.title: Microsoft Purview, governance and compliance
objectives: Describe the purpose of Microsoft Purview and its two main solution areas.
Recognise Purview's data governance capabilities: Data Map, Unified Catalog, classification and lineage.
Recognise Purview's risk and compliance capabilities: information protection, data loss prevention, insider risk, eDiscovery, audit and Compliance Manager.
Tell Purview apart from Azure Policy, Microsoft Defender for Cloud and Azure Monitor.
Pick the right tool for a governance or compliance scenario.
concepts: Microsoft Purview
A family of data governance, risk and compliance solutions that gives a single view of your data across on-premises, multicloud and SaaS sources.
Risk and compliance solutions
Protect and manage sensitive data in Microsoft 365 (Teams, OneDrive, SharePoint, Exchange), monitor how it is used, and manage risk.
Unified data governance
Discover, map and govern data across Azure, SQL, on-premises and other clouds such as Amazon S3.
Data Map
Scans registered sources and captures metadata so Purview can build an up-to-date map of the data estate.
Unified Catalog
Lets data consumers search for and understand trusted data, with business terms and ownership (formerly Data Catalog).
Classification
Automatically identifies data types such as credit card numbers or passport numbers, so sensitive data can be found wherever it is stored.
Data lineage
Shows where data came from and how it moved and changed between systems, end to end.
Sensitivity labels and DLP
Information protection labels classify and protect content. Data loss prevention policies help stop sensitive data being shared inappropriately.
Compliance Manager
Helps track regulatory requirements with assessments, improvement actions and a compliance score.
eDiscovery and Audit
Find content for legal cases, and search recorded user and admin activity.
comparisons: Purview governs data (what it is, where it is, who uses it). Azure Policy governs resource configuration (which resources can be deployed, and how).
Purview is about data governance and compliance. Defender for Cloud is about security posture and threat protection for workloads.
Purview maps and governs data. Azure Monitor collects metrics and logs about the performance and health of resources.
Data governance vs risk and compliance
Governance: map, catalog, classify and trace data. Risk and compliance: protect, retain, investigate and report on data.
traps: Purview doesn't stop someone deploying a VM in the wrong region. That's Azure Policy.
Purview isn't only for Azure data. It also scans on-premises, other clouds and SaaS sources.
Compliance score shows progress on improvement actions. It's not a certification of compliance.
Lineage traces data movement. It doesn't back data up.
Service Trust Portal is no longer an AZ-900 objective. Expect Purview instead.
revision: Purview = data governance + risk and compliance, in one family.
Data Map scans sources. Unified Catalog helps people find data. Classification finds sensitive data. Lineage traces it.
Sensitivity labels and DLP protect Microsoft 365 data.
Compliance Manager gives assessments, improvement actions and a compliance score.
Policy = resources. Purview = data. Defender for Cloud = security posture. Monitor = performance and health.
